taxonomy.subtopic: PML-RARA differentiation block, DIC, and all-trans retinoic acid

questions.stem_html:
A 31-year-old woman presents with gingival bleeding, fatigue, and widespread bruising. Platelets are 24,000/mm3, fibrinogen is low, and D-dimer is markedly elevated. A smear shows abnormal promyelocytes containing bundles of Auer rods. Cytogenetic analysis identifies t(15;17). Treatment is started immediately while supportive blood products are given.

How does the disease-specific therapy reverse the leukemic block?

options.text_html: Irreversible inhibition of DNA topoisomerase II causes selective apoptosis of mature neutrophils
Pharmacologic activation of the altered retinoic acid receptor permits terminal myeloid differentiation
Inhibition of BCR-ABL1 kinase restores normal granulocyte maturation
Blockade of dihydrofolate reductase eliminates the abnormal clone by nucleotide starvation

questions.explanation_html: PML-RARA recruits corepressors and prevents transcription of genes needed for myeloid maturation. All-trans retinoic acid overcomes this repression and promotes differentiation of leukemic promyelocytes. ATRA binds the abnormal retinoic acid receptor complex and releases the differentiation arrest; arsenic trioxide promotes degradation of the fusion protein.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: Topoisomerase inhibition is not the defining differentiation therapy for PML-RARA leukemia.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Promyelocytes are myeloid cells and do not characteristically express the B-cell marker CD20.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: BCR-ABL1 inhibition treats Philadelphia chromosome-positive disease, not t(15;17) APL.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Antifolate therapy is not the targeted mechanism of all-trans retinoic acid in APL.

questions.educational_objective: Identify APL as a coagulopathic emergency and explain how all-trans retinoic acid reverses the PML-RARA-mediated block in myeloid differentiation.
